title: Microsoft Teams: express voice enrollment from meeting audio
summary: The documented enrollment controls, user opt-in, data handling and roadmap details are supported. Minor corrections remain: the action rating understates a launched availability decision, and the checklist names controls absent from the controls table.

claims.claim: Express voice enrollment creates a Teams voice profile from speech during meetings.
claims.quote: For express enrollment, opt-in allows the Teams app to automatically capture users' voice data from Teams meetings and create and update their voice profile via their in-meeting speech.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The recognition profile is a person's biometric profile used to identify that enrolled person.
claims.quote:
Voice recognition: Uses an enrolled user’s voice profile to identify who is speaking in the room.
Voice and face recognition only works if end users have completed enrollment by creating their biometric profiles in Teams.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout and After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist instructs readers to allow a network endpoint, review enrollment status, delete profiles and check voice isolation, but these controls have no table rows.
claims.quote: Allow *.speech.microsoft.com on the network; Review enrolment status for your users in the Teams admin center, and delete profiles where required; Check that voice isolation and room recognition settings still match your intent. Rows cover only enrollment and room recognition.
claims.fix: Remove the At rollout bullet beginning 'Allow *.speech.microsoft.com' and the After rollout bullets beginning 'Review enrolment status' and 'Check that voice isolation'. Their factual descriptions may remain in Risk assessment and Governance controls; these checklist controls lack table rows.

claims.claim: The prepare action rating understates the decision for a launched, medium-risk feature offered without administrator action.
claims.quote: action: "prepare"; status: "launched"; risk: "medium"; Microsoft Learn documents the policy as enabled by default, so decide whether to leave it on or turn it off with PowerShell.
claims.fix: Set action to 'act-now': the change is launched, risk is medium, and administrators must decide whether to leave default enrollment availability enabled. Individual profile creation remains user-opt-in.
